name: Apple
summary: Hiring happens team by team, so loops vary widely. Expect depth in your area and close attention to detail.

process.note: Apple's careers pages describe its teams and culture but not the engineering interview loop. Every stage below is what candidates commonly report, so treat it as a rough outline.

stages.name: Recruiter or manager call
stages.detail: Candidates typically report a first call with a recruiter or the hiring manager about the team and role.

stages.name: Technical screens
stages.detail: Often one or two technical calls with team engineers, with coding or questions on your area.

stages.name: Team interviews
stages.detail: Several interviews with the team, often mixing coding, domain depth and a walk through past projects.

stages.name: Decision
stages.detail: The team usually decides; timelines vary by group.

design.note: Design questions are commonly reported for experienced roles and tend to follow the team's domain, such as media, sync or devices.

values.title: What Apple's careers pages emphasise
values.summary: Apple's careers pages stress original thinking, care for detail and a set of shared values such as accessibility, privacy, the environment and inclusion. The summaries are ours.

items.name: Care for the details
items.gist: Understand how things are made and sweat the small decisions.

items.name: Original thinking
items.gist: Bring the courage to propose ideas others might call too ambitious.

items.name: Privacy
items.gist: Treat user data as something to protect by design.

items.name: Accessibility
items.gist: Build for everyone, including people with disabilities.

items.name: Environment
items.gist: Weigh the environmental cost of what you make.

items.name: Inclusion
items.gist: Welcome different backgrounds and help everyone belong.

prompts.text: Describe a small detail you refused to let slide and why it mattered to users.
Tell a story where you pushed for an idea others thought was too ambitious.
Talk about a time you designed something to protect user data or privacy.
Share how you made a product or feature work for more people.

mock.note: Follows the team interviews as commonly reported: a coding round, a design deep dive and a conversation about past projects.
